title: Runtime contract markers and graceful deprecation playbook
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Introduce a contract-marker driven policy for the serving runtime that standardizes how we classify API/ABI changes, manage deprecation windows, and automate rollout/rollback decisions. This ticket captures the playbook, verification tooling, and telemetry thresholds required to ship breaking or potentially breaking changes with minimal customer impact.
background: We currently rely on semantic-major/minor patch decisions that are often ambiguous for surface-area changes (headers, optional fields, behavioral changes in KV cache). Incidents have shown gaps in: communicating precise compatibility guarantees, measuring client surface usage, and automating safe rollouts when a subtle client behavior regresses. Contract markers aim to make change intent explicit and machine-enforceable.
goals: Define a small set of runtime contract markers (Stable, Soft-Deprecation, Experimental, Breaking-Opt-In)
Build a contract manifest that ships with each runtime release and is exposed via API and sdk metadata
Enforce pre-merge compatibility checks using the contract manifest and downstream integration tests
Provide a standardized deprecation timeline (notice, soft-deprecation, hard-remove) and automated rollout gates tied to telemetry
Ship upgrade tooling (rwc-cli migration hint generator and SDK adapters) to reduce client upgrade effort
non_goals: Rewriting existing SDKs as part of this ticket
Replacing detailed API docs; this complements docs but does not duplicate them
proposal_summary: Attach lightweight contract markers to each endpoint/field and include a top-level runtime-contract.json in the release artifact. Markers express guarantees and expected client behavior. Changes that alter semantics must carry an elevated marker and trigger a deprecation workflow: announce (7 days), soft-deprecate (30 days auto-compat shim + telemetry), and hard-remove (90+ days) unless rollback criteria are met. Rollouts use canary cohorts and automated compatibility checks against customer usage patterns.
contract_markers: stable: backward-compatible; strong SLA; allowed in patch releases
soft-deprecation: compatible but flagged; servers may introduce warnings; clients should migrate
experimental: opt-in only; no compatibility guarantee; may be removed without notice
breaking-opt-in: new behavior behind explicit flag; default remains old behavior until runway completes
private-internal: internal-only API; not part of contract; may change freely
deprecation_policy_summary: Three-phase deprecation window: Notice (public announcement + migration guide), Soft-deprecation (compatibility shim and telemetry collection; non-breaking fallback), Hard-remove (actual removal after telemetry thresholds/timeout). Default windows: notice 7 days, soft 30 days, hard-remove earliest at 90 days; extension via PM approval for high-risk customers.
migration_strategy: Provide generated migration hints in change PRs via rwc-cli, a compatibility shim library in the runtime (server-side) and client adapters in SDKs to translate old payloads for 30 days. For major breaking changes, publish a migration-compat bundle and a step-by-step checklist per SDK.
rollout_gates: automated-canary: deploy to 5% of traffic with contract-enforcement enabled
compat-test-suite: run full backwards/forwards contract tests against stored request corpus
telemetry-thresholds: error-rate delta < 0.5% absolute and <20% relative over baseline
customer-impact-check: flag customers with high usage of the affected surface and delay removal if active
telemetry_and_alerting: contract-usage-metrics: per-endpoint/field usage counts exposed in Console
compatibility-failures: histogram of requests requiring shim or failing after change
anomaly-alert: triggered when error-rate delta exceeds thresholds during canary
rollback-signal: automated rollback if compat failures sustained for >15 minutes in canary
upgrade_tooling_changes: rwc-cli: new 'rwc contract-diff' command to show marker deltas and generate migration hints
sdk-adapters: lightweight adapters to opt-in to breaking behavior via explicit flags
ci-hook: pre-merge contract check that refuses PRs which change a stable marker without RFC approval
runtime: embed runtime-contract.json in the docker image and expose /internal/contract for infra checks
acceptance_criteria: runtime-contract.json schema checked into repo and validated by unit tests
rwc-cli contract-diff returns human-friendly migration hints in change PRs
CI blocks merges that demote stable markers without RFC-approved override
Canary rollout exercises contract gates and telemetry emits the defined metrics
Docs published and console surfaces per-endpoint contract usage counts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly conservative markers slow innovation. Mitigation: allow Experimental and Breaking-Opt-In markers for rapid iteration.
Risk: Customers miss notices. Mitigation: send targeted Console notifications and email to tenants with dependency mappings.
Risk: Telemetry gaps for edge cases. Mitigation: require runtime to capture request hashes for failing cases (privacy-reviewed) and retain for 7 days.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (2 sprints): schema + rwc-cli + CI hook + small runtime endpoint to expose contract manifest
Phase 2 (2 sprints): server-side shims, canary automation, console telemetry visualization
Phase 3 (opt): SDK adapters and migration campaign with Support for top 20 customers
Coordinate with PMs to define default windows and exceptions workflow
